## Overview

This project packages **four modern fine-tuning techniques** into **two runnable local pipelines** for consumer GPUs (16–24 GB VRAM):

| Project | Model | Method | Best for |
|---------|-------|--------|----------|
| **Speed Run** | Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | **QLoRA + Unsloth** | Domain format, API syntax, corporate knowledge |
| **Preference Align** | Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | **ORPO + DoRA** | Tone, safety, chosen vs rejected responses |

**GitHub:** [sophalchan/modern-llm-finetuning-lab](https://github.com/sophalchan/modern-llm-finetuning-lab)

**Stack:** PyTorch · Unsloth · PEFT · TRL · bitsandbytes · Hugging Face

## The 4 techniques (plain English)

| Technique | What it does |
|-----------|----------------|
| **QLoRA** | Keeps the big model in 4-bit; trains only tiny adapter layers → fits on one GPU |
| **Unsloth** | Faster training kernels → 2–5× speed, ~60% less memory |
| **ORPO** | Aligns preferences in **one step** (no separate SFT then DPO) |
| **DoRA** | Updates direction and magnitude separately → closer to full fine-tune quality |

## Background of the Study

Full fine-tuning of 7B–8B models on a laptop GPU is impractical. The industry moved to **parameter-efficient** methods: train adapters, not every weight. **QLoRA** made 8B models reachable on 16 GB cards; **Unsloth** made training fast enough for iteration; **ORPO** simplified preference alignment; **DoRA** improved adapter quality without full-parameter cost.

This lab turns those ideas into **copy-paste scripts** with YAML configs—aligned with my AI engineering work (Krulabs.ai local LLM prep, AI Lecturer labs on LoRA/QLoRA/RAG).

## Motivation of the Study

- **Run locally** on consumer hardware instead of cloud-only fine-tuning  
- **Compare two real use cases:** domain SFT vs preference alignment  
- **Use community-standard tools** (Unsloth, TRL ORPO, PEFT DoRA)  
- **Export adapters** for inference and optional GGUF (Ollama / LM Studio)  
- **Document GPU requirements** honestly—8B training needs CUDA  

## Project 1 — Llama-3.1-8B + Unsloth QLoRA

Teaches formatting, instructions, or domain text quickly.

```bash
pip install -r requirements-base.txt
pip install "unsloth[colab-new] @ git+https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth.git"
python project1_unsloth_qlora/train_llama31_unsloth.py
python project1_unsloth_qlora/infer_llama31_unsloth.py
python project1_unsloth_qlora/export_gguf.py
```

Config: `configs/project1_unsloth_qlora.yaml` · Output: `lora_model_llama3/`

## Project 2 — Qwen + ORPO + DoRA (8GB GPU config)

Uses **chosen vs rejected** pairs for style and safety alignment in one training pass.

```bash
python project2_orpo_dora/train_qwen_orpo.py --config project2_low_vram.yaml
python project2_orpo_dora/infer_qwen_orpo.py
python app_ui.py   # Web UI → http://localhost:7860
```

Config: `configs/project2_low_vram.yaml` · Output: `orpo_qwen_final/`

## Web UI — test in your browser

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install gradio
python app_ui.py
```

Open **http://localhost:7860** — Gradio chat with example prompts, temperature slider, and max-token control.

## Environment check

```bash
python scripts/check_environment.py
```

Set `HF_TOKEN` in `.env` for gated models (Llama 3.1).

## Hardware note

| Requirement | Detail |
|-------------|--------|
| GPU | NVIDIA — **8 GB** works (Project 2 + low_vram config); **16 GB+** for 8B models |
| OS | Linux + CUDA (Unsloth optimized for Linux) |
| Disk | ~20 GB+ for model weights cache |

Scripts are validated locally; **full training runs on a CUDA machine** (not CPU-only).
